newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Fuel Oil- Firm with a deal traded at $100/T.
newsitem.headline: Asia Fuel Oil- Firm with a deal traded at $100/T.

text.p: Singapore high sulphur fuel oil prices edged higher on firm bids and fresh tender demand from Taiwan and India, traders said on Thursday.
A 20,000 tonne cargo of 180-centistoke fuel oil market was sold by a Japanese shosha to a local trader for May 2-6 loading at $100 per tonne, fob.
Prices rose by $1 per tonne from a bid seen on Wednesday at $99.00 per tonne.
Traders said the local trader who had purchased the cargo is expected to buy more next week.
Spot tender demand from Taiwan and India has helped boost sentiment.
Taiwan has issued a six month tender to buy up to two 38,000 tonne cargoes per month of fuel oil between June and November.
India has also issued a tender to buy 30,000 tonnes of 180-centistoke fuel oil for delivery May 6-10.
The rise in levels is despite an increase in residual feedstocks. Singapore Trade Development Board statistics showed a rise of 638,000 barrels to 10.692 million barrels.
Talks were heard that a French major is bringing a Venezuelan cargoes to Asia, but some traders said the cargo has already been sold.
South Korea is expected to export only about five to six cargoes of fuel oil in May. Chinese enquiries were heard active in South Korean market at around $7-$8 per tonne over Singapore spot quotes.
LSWR market is quiet with traders saying that there are ample of supplies in the prompt market.
(Prices in dollars per tonne, unless stated)
